title: Linear smoothers
html:
Call f^=Sy a linear smoother with smoother matrix S when S does not depend on y. The estimators of @def-smo-kernel, @def-smo-pspline and @thm-smo-smoothing-spline are linear smoothers, with S given by @eq-smo-equivalent, @eq-smo-smoother and @eq-smo-reinsch-fit. Suppose E(Y)=f and Cov(Y)=σ2I. Then:

  1. (Moments.) E(f^)=Sf, Cov(f^)=σ2SS⊤, and E‖f^−f‖2=‖(I−S)f‖2+σ2tr(SS⊤).{#eq-smo-risk}

  2. (Residuals.) E‖y−f^‖2=‖(I−S)f‖2+σ2{n−2tr(S)+tr(SS⊤)}, so σ^2=‖y−f^‖2n−2tr(S)+tr(SS⊤){#eq-smo-sigma-hat}

    is unbiased for σ2 when the bias term is negligible.

  3. (Degrees of freedom.) If S is symmetric with eigenvalues in [0,1] — as it is for a penalized or smoothing spline, by @prp-smo-pspline-ridge(b) — then tr(SS⊤)≤tr(S)≤2tr(S)−tr(SS⊤), with equality throughout iff S is an orthogonal projection, in which case all three equal its rank.

  4. (Shrinkage.) For a penalized spline, @eq-smo-smoother writes Sλ in the Demmler–Reinsch basis as a diagonal shrinkage uj⊤y↦uj⊤y/(1+λej): smooth directions (ej small) pass through, rough ones are damped. The smoothing spline has the same form with ej the eigenvalues of the roughness matrix relative to the identity.

  5. (Pointwise bands.) f^(xi)±z1−α/2σ^(SS⊤)ii is an interval for E{f^(xi)}=(Sf)i, not for f(xi). Its coverage of f(xi) is 1−α only to the extent that the bias {(S−I)f}i is small next to σ(SS⊤)ii.
